## Outcome

Make `/admin/members` reflow across viewport widths so account-state tabs, pending counts, member details, status badges, and member actions remain readable, separated, visible, and usable without overlap or horizontal page overflow.

## Scope Boundary

### Included

- Responsive presentation of the existing account-state tabs and pending counts.
- Responsive presentation of each existing member row and its status and role actions.
- Focused automated regression checks using the existing member feature coverage.
- Targeted authenticated responsive review at 320px, 375px, 390px, 768px, and 1280px when the local review capability is available.
- Run evidence and relevant PM Control traceability.

### Excluded

- Account-state classification, pending-count calculation, search, pagination, or URL filter behavior.
- Approve, revoke, restore, or Change role server actions.
- Authentication, authorization, participant-data handling, routes, database schema, storage, email, deployment, staging, or production configuration.
- New member-management features or changes to the approved account-state scope.

## Approved Traceability

- `RQ-08 (The application must work on desktop, tablet, and mobile devices)` supplies the responsive acceptance boundary.
- `RQ-09 (Administrators must approve, grant, revoke, and restore participant access)` supplies the existing member-action behavior that must remain usable.
- `RQ-10 (Protected routes, APIs, and files must enforce server-side access controls)` remains unchanged and must not be weakened.
- `RQ-15 (The application should support participant, moderator, and administrator permissions)` remains unchanged.
- `CHG-46 (Separate administrator member lists by account state)` is the approved parent change.
- `D-69 (Should the administrator Members page separate users by account state?)` is the existing made decision authorizing the four state views and preservation of member behavior.
- `ACT-66 (Implement and verify administrator account-state tabs and pending counts)` remains the parent implementation action and stays open for broader acceptance.
- `LL-14 (Build member administration, access approval, revocation, restoration, and permission management, with exclusive account-state views and live pending counts)` is the related backlog item.
- `LL-23 (Test authentication, roles, registration, account-state views, counts, access transitions, and direct unauthorized requests)`, `LL-24 (Test member and application feature workflows)`, and `LL-25 (Test desktop, tablet, and mobile workflows)` provide the test boundary.

## Implementation Boundary

The expected production change is a page-scoped responsive layout correction in `application/source/resources/js/pages/admin/members/index.tsx`. The implementation must keep the four existing tabs, labels, counts, content, actions, and server contracts. Shared UI primitives should not change unless Design and Build show that a page-scoped correction cannot satisfy the acceptance conditions.

### Responsive and Accessibility

- Review the authenticated `/admin/members` page at 320px, 375px, 390px, 768px, and 1280px.
- Confirm every state tab and pending count is readable and focusable without overlap.
- Confirm the active tab content starts below the tab list.
- Confirm member identity, status, Approve access, Revoke access, Restore access, and Change role controls reflow within the viewport and remain reachable.
- Confirm no horizontal page overflow and no control is hidden behind another element.
- Confirm the existing search and state-filter interactions still preserve their visible content.
- Use synthetic local accounts only. Do not capture or store real participant data.

If authenticated browser review is unavailable, record that exact limitation in Build and Measure. Do not claim the responsive acceptance condition as passed from source inspection alone.

## Risks and Controls

| Risk | Control |
|---|---|
| A narrow layout fix hides or clips a member action. | Check each action at all target widths and retain automated access-transition coverage. |
| A tab layout correction changes the existing state or count behavior. | Leave the controller and route contract unchanged and rerun the focused member suite. |
| A shared primitive change creates unrelated regressions. | Prefer page-scoped classes and run the broader frontend checks. |
| Local visual evidence is mistaken for staging or launch acceptance. | Keep staging, HTTPS, operations, participant-data, and launch gates open in the handoff. |

## Rollback

Revert the page-scoped layout change in `application/source/resources/js/pages/admin/members/index.tsx` to the recorded pre-change commit. No migration, data, route, or deployment rollback is required. Keep the existing Members workflow and SharePoint fallback available.
